questions.q: Why does the lesson argue that a check only run when someone remembers to isn't a real quality program?
options: It's a habit that will eventually lapse, often right when something actually breaks
SQL Server does not allow a query to be run more than once manually
Manual checks always produce incorrect results
A check must be automated before it can be written in T-SQL at all
questions.explain: The lesson's core argument is that automation turns detection from 'sometimes' into 'always' — a manually run check is only as reliable as someone's memory and habits, which tend to lapse.

questions.q: Why doesn't a plain `SELECT` statement that returns violating rows cause a SQL Server Agent job step to show as Failed?
options: A job step is only marked Failed when the T-SQL actually raises an error, such as with RAISERROR or THROW
SQL Server Agent cannot execute SELECT statements at all
A SELECT statement always returns a success code regardless of its row count
Job steps can only fail if they contain a syntax error
questions.explain: SQL Server Agent judges a job step's success or failure based on whether the T-SQL raised an error, not based on the content of a result set. A SELECT that simply returns rows — even many — does not, by itself, fail the step.

questions.q: What is the purpose of pairing a job's failure with an operator and a notification?
options: So the right person is alerted automatically the moment a threshold is crossed, rather than whenever they next happen to check
So the job runs faster
So the RAISERROR statement is no longer needed
So the check no longer needs to be scheduled
questions.explain: A configured operator and notification turn a failed job state into an actual alert sent to a responsible person, closing the loop between detection and someone knowing about it.

questions.q: What does Azure Data Factory's Validation activity do, as described in the lesson?
options: It pauses the pipeline itself until a dataset reference is confirmed to exist and meet defined criteria, or times out
It automatically repairs invalid rows found during a pipeline run
It replaces the need for any SQL Server Agent jobs in a data platform
It only works with on-premises SQL Server, never cloud data sources
questions.explain: The Validation activity gates pipeline execution on a dataset condition — delaying or stopping downstream activities until the dataset exists and meets the specified criteria, or the activity times out.

questions.q: According to the lesson, when is a SQL Server Agent job the right default over a pipeline-native validation activity?
options: When every table involved in the check lives within the same SQL Server environment
Whenever the check needs to block downstream pipeline activities from running
Only when the check involves fewer than 100 rows
SQL Server Agent and Validation activities can never be used in the same data platform
questions.explain: The lesson distinguishes the two by scope and purpose: SQL Server Agent fits checks fully inside one SQL Server environment, while a pipeline-native Validation activity fits when the check needs to gate whether downstream pipeline steps execute at all — and notes real platforms often use both.
